<coding_guidelines>
# AGENTS.md

How agents work in this repository. The rules are in [ai/RULES.md](ai/RULES.md) and win over
anything here; this file is the operational summary.

## What this is

droid-observatory: a Tauri 2 + Leptos (Rust) desktop app that shows a Factory Mission moving
through nine lanes, with validation, gate, agent attribution, waste and cost per sub-droid.
PRD: `ai/prd/droid-observatory-prd.md`. Spec: `SPEC.md` (approved 2026-10-22; the mission plans from it).

Current state: the walking skeleton (core crate, canonical `Event`, `observatory-cli replay` over
one captured session, an empty board that starts) is integrated on `mission/observatory-v1`
(2026-10-23). Each later milestone deepens one area from it.

## Setup, build, test

```sh
make doctor          # tool check with install hints
make hooks           # enable .githooks (once)
make check           # all light checks = mission-branch CI
make fmt             # rustfmt (no-op until Cargo.toml exists)
make lint            # clippy -D warnings
make test            # cargo test --workspace
make deny            # cargo-deny advisories, licences, bans
make replay-fixtures # observatory-cli replay over fixtures/streams/*.jsonl
make app-dev         # Tauri dev window (after the app exists)
```

Toolchain: `rust-toolchain.toml` (1.99.1, rustfmt, clippy, wasm32 target). Do not change it
without a decision file.

## Runtime limits (measured)

Measured 2026-10-22 on the owner's machine; source `reports/readiness/2026-10-22-validation-readiness.md`
(SPEC §5.8):

- At most 3 concurrent agent-browser validator sessions per `trunk serve` (1.34-1.54 GB RSS each,
  CPU negligible idle); use `--session <name>` per validator.
- `cargo llvm-cov` runs alone (1-min load 3.3 → 14.6 on 10 cores during the scratch run).
- All cargo builds serialize on the shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` lock
  (`Blocking waiting for file lock on build directory`); expect waits, not failures.
- `trunk serve` and `cargo tauri dev` coexist only when exactly one trunk owns port 3141
  (`cargo tauri dev` starts its own); killing `cargo-tauri` alone orphans trunk and the app binary.
- Cold `trunk serve` 55.94 s, incremental 1.46-2.08 s, `cargo tauri dev` to running app 37.66 s.
- The Tauri window has no CDP endpoint; validators use the smoke check (process alive, `Running`
  log line, WebKit connections on 3141, System Events listing) plus the browser path on 3141.

## Interactive QA path

Until the app exists: `make check` is the only runnable target.
Once the skeleton lands, the path the validators follow is:

1. `make doctor` reports no missing required tools.
2. `cargo run -p observatory-cli -- replay fixtures/streams/<capture>.jsonl` prints lane
   events and ends with `unknown events: N`: `2027` on the S fixture
   (`2026-10-22-observatory-v1-s.jsonl`, the mapper knows no kind yet), `0` from the M0 fixture
   onward.
3. `make app-dev` opens the window; open the same fixture (Replay); the nine lanes render
   and a card opens its Details view.
4. With the window open, start `droid exec --mission ...` in a terminal; the new session
   appears on the board (Attach) and each event shows within 1 s.

No login gate: the app watches and reads local session files and uses the GitHub token from the keychain or
`GITHUB_TOKEN` only for the gate lane.

## Layout and ownership

```text
crates/observatory-core   ingest, model, metrics, store, control (no UI deps)
crates/observatory-cli    headless replay/inspect over core
apps/observatory-app      Tauri 2 shell + Leptos UI
fixtures/streams          captured mission streams, named <YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.jsonl
docs/decisions            D-NNN-slug.md, one per decision; README.md is generated
docs/runbooks             recovery procedures: red gate, fix cycle, stall, hooks, release
reports/                  usage, waste, readiness; pasted from tools
build-log/                tool-call log written by .factory hooks
ai/                       PRD, rules, template, session logs
```

Crate and app paths are the contract the Makefile and CI probe for; keep them.

## Conventions

- Rust 2024 edition, `rustfmt.toml` and `clippy.toml` as committed. Warnings are errors.
- Naming: standard Rust (`snake_case` items and modules, `CamelCase` types, `SCREAMING_SNAKE`
  consts). Event kinds mirror the PRD §7 names in `snake_case`
  (`finding.blocking` → `FindingBlocking`). Lane and role enums use the PRD's words.
- Tests: unit tests in `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` next to the code; integration tests in
  `crates/<crate>/tests/<topic>.rs`; fixture-driven tests read `fixtures/streams/`. Test
  functions read as sentences: `rework_window_closes_on_resolution()`.
- Tests before code (rule 1): commit the red test, then the code that turns it green.
- No magic numbers: every threshold lives in `config/observatory.example.toml` with a reason.
- Debt markers: `TODO(#123)` or `TODO(B-123)`; anything else fails `make check-todos`.
- Markdown: `.markdownlint-cli2.yaml`; links must resolve (`make check-links`).
- Files over 200 KB fail CI unless under `fixtures/streams/` or `build-log/`.

## Git

- Forward only (rule 12): never amend, reset, rebase, stash, or force-push. Fix with a new
  commit. `.factory/hooks/guard-git.sh` and `.githooks/pre-push` enforce this.
- Nothing reaches `main` except the mission's single pull request. `main` has a ruleset:
  PR required, `gate` check required, no force push, no bypass.
- Milestones live in worktrees and integrate into `mission/<name>`. Two worktrees never edit
  the same file (rule 13); shared files (`SPEC.md` §9–10, `README.md`, `BACKLOG.md`,
  `docs/decisions/README.md`) are written by the orchestrator at integration time.
- Commit subject under 72 characters; co-author trailer for agent commits:
  `Co-authored-by: factory-droid[bot] <138933559+factory-droid[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>`.

## Decisions, backlog, logs

- A decision is one file: `docs/decisions/D-NNN-slug.md` with `**Date:**`, `**Status:**`,
  context, decision, alternatives, consequences. Run `make decisions-index` after adding one.
- Deferred work goes to `BACKLOG.md` as `B-NNN` with a reason, not into TODOs or GitHub issues
  (rule 14; owner decision 2026-10-22 at mission approval).
- Every session is logged under `ai/session/` with transcript links; every tool call is
  logged to `build-log/` by the PostToolUse hook. Do not disable the hooks.
- Usage and waste per milestone go to `reports/` pasted from the tool that produced them.

## Mission setup

Models per role (rule 19; `.factory/settings.json`; D-006):

| Role | Model |
|---|---|
| Orchestrator | `claude-fable-5.1` |
| Workers | `claude-sonnet-5-5` |
| Validators (scrutiny, user testing) | `claude-opus-5-5` |

Command: see README "Running it as a mission".
Reasoning effort: orchestrator `high`, workers `high`, validators `high` (SPEC §2).
A model change is a decision file.

The human answers only at milestone boundaries or when the stall flag is up (rule 15).
Deviations from the spec are proposed with reason and cost, and wait for approval (rule 9).

## Environment and secrets

See `.env.example`. Secrets come from the OS keychain (`droid-observatory/<name>` entries)
or the environment, never from the repository, the store, or logs. Raw session JSONL may
contain secrets: render read-only, never upload, never copy into the store.

- The GitHub token is a read-only fine-grained PAT; read check results via Actions runs
  (`/repos/{o}/{r}/actions/runs`) and commit statuses (`/repos/{o}/{r}/commits/{sha}/status`), not the
  Checks API (no Checks permission). Keychain items are generic passwords with service
  `droid-observatory/<name>` (see `reports/readiness/2026-10-22-dependency-readiness.md`).

Grafana Cloud OTLP (`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*`) is the telemetry backend; export is off unless
`[telemetry].enabled = true`.

## Do not

- Add a dependency without `make deny` passing and a version verified on the day (rule 3).
- Write to `main`, rewrite history, or touch another worktree's files.
- Estimate a count, timing or token number: paste it from the tool (rule 7).
- Drop an unknown event: count it and show it (rule 18).
</coding_guidelines>

# Worker Base Procedures

You are a worker in a multi-agent mission. This skill defines the procedures that ALL workers must follow. After completing startup, you'll invoke your specific worker skill for the actual work procedure.

## Your Assigned Feature

Your feature has been pre-assigned by the system and is shown in your bootstrap message. The feature includes:
- `id` - Feature identifier
- `description` - What to build
- `skillName` - The skill you must invoke for the work procedure
- `expectedBehavior` - What success looks like
- `fulfills` - Validation contract assertion IDs (if present)

**Your feature's `fulfills` field lists validation contract assertions that must be true after your work.** Read these assertions carefully before starting — they define what "done" means for your feature. Before completing, ensure that each assertion would pass. If you realize an assertion cannot be fulfilled given your current scope, flag it in your handoff.

**Explicit technology choices are binding.** If the user or orchestrator specified a package, library, SDK, or tool for this mission or feature, you must use that exact choice. Do not swap in an alternative because it seems easier, is already installed, or avoids an allowlist problem. If the specified dependency is unavailable or blocked, return to the orchestrator instead of substituting.


## Service Management via Manifest

`services.yaml` is the **single source of truth** for all commands and services.

**Using the manifest:**
- Read it to find commands/services
- For services: use `start`, `stop`, `healthcheck` commands exactly as declared
- For commands: use named commands (e.g., `commands.test`)

**Starting services:**
1. Check `depends_on` and start dependencies first
2. Run the `start` command from the manifest
3. Wait for `healthcheck` to pass (retry a few times with backoff)
4. If healthcheck fails to succeed within a reasonable timeframe → return to orchestrator immediately with a report.

**Stopping services:**
- Use the manifest's `stop` command (which uses the declared port)
- Port-based kills are ALLOWED when using the manifest's declared port

**If manifest is broken:** Return to orchestrator with `returnToOrchestrator: true` - don't try to fix it yourself.

## CRITICAL: Never Kill User Processes

**FORBIDDEN commands:**
- `pkill node`, `killall`, `kill` by process name
- Port-based kills on ports NOT declared in `services.yaml`
- Any command that kills processes you didn't start

**ALLOWED:**
- Port-based kills using the manifest's declared `stop` command (these use declared ports)
- Killing processes by PID that YOU started in this session

Port conflict on a port NOT in the manifest? Return to orchestrator. NEVER kill the existing process.

(CRITICAL) If you discovered reusable services or commands that future workers will need, ADD them to `services.yaml`. See Phase 3.3 for details.

## Phase 1: Startup

### 1.1 Read Context

**PERFORMANCE TIP:** Parallelize your startup by reading all context files in a single tool call batch. The files below are independent and can be read simultaneously along with invoking your worker skill. This significantly reduces startup time.

Read these to understand the mission state:

- `mission.md` - The accepted mission proposal representing the full scope and strategy agreed upon between orchestrator and user
- `architecture.md` (top level of missionDir) - The system's authoritative architecture. Mandatory reading for you to understand how your work fits into the larger system.
- `AGENTS.md` - Guidance from the orchestrator and user. **Includes Mission Boundaries (port ranges, external services, off-limits resources) that you must NEVER violate.** May be updated mid-run with new user instructions - always check for latest guidance.
- If your feature has `fulfills`, read those specific assertions from `validation-contract.md` — they define the exact behavior your implementation must satisfy.
- `services.yaml` - How to run commands and services (single source of truth for operations)
- `features.json` - Feature list (`jq '.features[:5] | map({id, description, status, milestone, skillName})' features.json`)
- `git log --oneline -20` - Recent commit history to see what's been done

Also available for reference:
- `library/` - Other knowledge base files written by previous workers (organized by topic).

(CRITICAL) The following documents are critical:
- `AGENTS.md`:
  - **Includes Mission Boundaries (port ranges, external services, off-limits resources) that you must NEVER violate.**
  - This may be updated mid-mission with new user instructions - always check for latest guidance.
- `services.yaml`:
  - **Single source of truth for all commands and services.** Do not start services any other way. If an entry is broken, return to orchestrator.

Ignoring these could be catastrophic for the mission's result. **Violating mission boundaries could damage the user's system or other projects.**

### 1.2 Initialize Environment

1. Run `init.sh` if it exists (one-time setup, idempotent)

If init fails:
- Call EndFeatureRun with `returnToOrchestrator: true` and explain the failure

### 1.3 Understand The Architecture

Read `architecture.md` to understand the system's architecture and how your feature fits into it. This is mandatory reading. It provides the context you need to make informed decisions during implementation, understand where to add new code, and how to integrate with existing components.

### 1.4 Understand Your Feature's Context

Your feature is has been assigned to you in the user message. View all features in your feature's milestone to understand the full context:

```bash
jq --arg m "YOUR_MILESTONE" '.features | map(select(.milestone == $m)) | map({id, description, status})' {missionDir}/features.json
```

Replace `YOUR_MILESTONE` with the actual milestone name from your assigned feature. This shows all features (any status) in the milestone so you understand what's been done, what's in progress, and what's pending.

### 1.5 Check Library

You have access to `library/`, which contains knowledge from the orchestrator and previous workers. The library is organized by topic. It may include guidance or docs for specific technologies you will be using. Refer to these for technology-specific idiomatic patterns, SDK usage, and anti-patterns.

### 1.6 Online Research (Conditional)

If your feature involves a technology, SDK, or integration where you're not confident about the correct idiomatic patterns — and `library/` doesn't already cover it — do an online lookup (WebSearch/FetchUrl) to verify the correct usage before implementing.

### 1.7 Start Services

Start any services you'll need from `services.yaml`:

- Check `depends_on` and start dependencies first
- Run each service's `start` command
- Wait for `healthcheck` to pass before proceeding
- If ANY service fails to start or healthcheck fails → return to orchestrator immediately

---

## Code Quality Principles

These are non-negotiable. Apply them throughout your work:

- **Avoid god files** - If a file is growing large, split it into focused modules
- **Create reusable components** - Don't duplicate code; extract and reuse
- **Keep changes focused** - Don't sprawl across unrelated areas
- **Stay in scope** - Record unrelated issues and optional improvements in your report or `salientSummary`, not as unfinished assigned work. Reserve `discoveredIssues` for concrete defects or blockers needing action. Check `{missionDir}/AGENTS.md` for "Known Pre-Existing Issues" to avoid re-reporting; do not go off-track to fix them.

---

## Phase 2: Work (Defined by Your Specific Skill)

After completing startup, invoke the skill specified in your feature's `skillName` field.

**If the skill does not exist** (i.e., the Skill tool returns an error), do not proceed with the work. Instead, return to the orchestrator immediately by calling EndFeatureRun with `returnToOrchestrator: true` and explain that the specified skill does not exist.

That skill will guide you through the actual work procedure.

---

## Phase 3: Cleanup & Handoff

After completing the work procedure, you MUST clean up and report.

### 3.1 Final Validation

Before cleanup, run the verification step(s) defined in your worker skill's Work Procedure. Fix any failures your work introduced. Do not hand off with broken verification.

### 3.2 Environment Cleanup

Before calling EndFeatureRun, stop all services you started:

1. **Stop services using manifest commands**: For each service you started, run its `stop` command from `services.yaml`
2. **Stop any other processes YOU started**: By their specific PID (not by port or name)
3. **Ensure clean git status in repos you changed**: Commit or stash repository changes. MissionDir artifact-only changes do not need commits.

The manifest's `stop` commands use declared ports, so port-based kills are safe for those. Do NOT kill processes on ports not declared in the manifest.

### 3.3 Add Any Services/Commands Discovered to the Manifest

If you discovered reusable services or commands that future workers will need, ADD them to `services.yaml`.

**Updating the manifest:**

If you discover a new service or command that future workers will need, you may add it to `services.yaml`:

1. **If service uses a port**: the port MUST be hardcoded in ALL commands (`start`, `stop`, `healthcheck`) AND in the `port` field
2. **Add the service/command** with required fields:
  - For services: `start`, `stop`, `healthcheck` (port hardcoded in command string), `port` (for conflict detection - not auto-injected), `depends_on`
  - For commands: just the command string

Example - adding a new service:
```yaml
services:
  # ... existing services ...
  storybook:
    start: PORT=6006 npm run storybook
    stop: lsof -ti :6006 | xargs kill
    healthcheck: curl -sf http://localhost:6006
    port: 6006
    depends_on: []
```

### 3.4 Call EndFeatureRun

Report your results. Your specific worker skill defines what a thorough handoff looks like - follow its Example Handoff.

Keep optional recommendations out of `discoveredIssues` and `whatWasLeftUndone`: those fields interrupt execution and require orchestrator action. Record recommendations in the report and reference it in `salientSummary`. Never hide a concrete unmet requirement or validation blocker this way. Report actual commands, exit codes, and limitations; `validatorsPassed: true` requires successful required checks, not a renamed failure or a check you did not run.

```
EndFeatureRun({
  successState: "success" | "failure",
  returnToOrchestrator: boolean,
  commitId: "...",           // include when repository code changed
  repoPath: "/path/to/repo",  // include with commitId
  validatorsPassed: boolean, // required true if success
  handoff: {
    salientSummary: "...",  // 1–4 sentences
    whatWasImplemented: "...",
    whatWasLeftUndone: "",   // empty if truly complete
    verification: {
      commandsRun: [{ command, exitCode, observation }],
      interactiveChecks: [{ action, observed }]  // for UI/browser work
    },
    tests: {
      added: [{ file, cases: [{ name, description }] }],
      coverage: "..."
    },
    discoveredIssues: [{ severity, description, suggestedFix? }],
    skillFeedback: {
      followedProcedure: true,  // or false if you deviated
      deviations: [],           // details if followedProcedure is false
      suggestedChanges: []      // optional improvements
    }
  }
})
```

#### Verification Hygiene

When running validators or tests during your work:
- **Do NOT pipe output through `| tail`, `| head`, or similar** — pipes mask the real exit code. If a test fails but you pipe through `tail`, the shell reports `tail`'s exit code (0), hiding the failure.
- **Prefer narrower test selection over output truncation.** If output is too noisy, run a more targeted test pattern (e.g., `npm test -- --testPathPattern MyFile`) instead of piping through `head`/`tail`.

#### Skill Feedback (help improve future workers)

Before calling EndFeatureRun, reflect on whether you followed your skill's procedure:

- **Did you follow the procedure as written?** If yes, set `followedProcedure: true` and leave `deviations` empty.
- **Did you deviate?** If you did something differently than the skill instructed, record it:
  - `step`: Which step (e.g., "Run tests before commit")
  - `whatIDidInstead`: What you actually did
  - `why`: Why you deviated (skill was unclear, found a better approach, blocked by environment, etc.)

This feedback helps the orchestrator improve skills for future milestones. Be honest -- deviations aren't failures, they're data.

#### When to Return to Orchestrator

Set `returnToOrchestrator: true` when:

- **Cannot complete work within mission boundaries** - if the feature requires violating boundaries (port range, off-limits resources), return immediately. NEVER violate boundaries.
- **Service won't start or healthcheck fails** - manifest may be broken or external dependency missing
- **Dependency or service that SHOULD exist is inaccessible** - if something that was working before (database, API, external service, file, etc.) is no longer accessible and you cannot figure out how to restore it after investigation, return immediately. Do not spin endlessly trying to fix infrastructure issues you can't resolve.
- Blocked by missing dependency, unsatisfied preconditions, or unclear requirements
- Previous worker left broken state you can't fix
- Decision or input needed from human/orchestrator
- Your skill type requires it.

#### When You Cannot Validate Your Work

If you cannot actually verify your work because of an environment or access blocker — e.g. the app is logged out and you can't authenticate, a page won't load, a service is unreachable, credentials are expired, or the agent-browser session never becomes ready — you must NOT report `successState: "success"`, and you must NOT silently defer the unverifiable check into a vague follow-up feature for "later".

Instead:
- Call EndFeatureRun with `successState: "failure"` (or `"partial"` if some assertions were genuinely verified) and `returnToOrchestrator: true`.
- Put the exact blocker, what you tried, and which assertions remain unverified in `handoff.salientSummary` and `handoff.discoveredIssues` (severity `blocking`).

Reporting a clear, blocking failure (instead of deferring the unverifiable check) is what lets the blocker get fixed or escalated to the user.

**CRITICAL: After calling EndFeatureRun, you MUST end your turn immediately. Do not continue with additional work, do not start another feature, do not make any further tool calls. Your session is complete once you call EndFeatureRun.**
</skill>

## Never

  number, create GitHub issues, or change a model/effort setting.

# AGENTS.md — droid-observatory v1 mission

Operational guidance for every worker and validator. Precedence: `ai/RULES.md` (repo) > this file's
boundaries > `planning-notes.md` (owner decisions after the spec) > `SPEC.md` v0.2 > PRD v0.6. The design
is `architecture.md`; the definition of done is `validation-contract.md`. Commands and services live in
`services.yaml`. Mission objectives are in `mission.md`, not here.

## Mission Boundaries (NEVER VIOLATE)

**Repository and branches**
- Repo: `/home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/droid-observatory`, mission branch `mission/observatory-v1`.
- Implementation workers and validators work ONLY in the active worktree
  `/home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/observatory-wt/current` → `../observatory-wt/<m>` on `wt/<m>`.
  Only the `integration-worker` (and the orchestrator) touches the main checkout and the shared files
  `SPEC.md`, `README.md`, `BACKLOG.md`, `docs/decisions/README.md` (workers may regenerate it with
  `make decisions-index` after adding a decision file, because milestones are sequential), `reports/`, `ai/session/`.
- Never write to `main`, never touch ruleset `main-gate` (id 25636994), never open or merge a PR to `main`
  (the orchestrator opens the single final PR; the owner merges it).
- Git is forward-only: no amend, reset, rebase, stash, force-push, `--no-verify`, or hook changes. Hooks
  `.githooks/*` and `.factory/hooks.json` stay enabled. Commit subject ≤ 72 chars, trailer
  `Co-authored-by: factory-droid[bot] <138933559+factory-droid[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>`.
- `rust-toolchain.toml` (1.99.1) and `.factory/settings.json` (models/effort) change only by decision file
  approved by the owner. No silent model or reasoning-effort change, ever.

**Ports**: 3141 for the UI dev server (exactly one `trunk serve` owns it); 3142–3149 scratch. Off-limits:
5000, 7000, 8000 (SurrealDB), 11434 (Ollama), 18444–18451, and anything already listening
(check `lsof -nP -iTCP:<port> -sTCP:LISTEN` before binding).

**Off-limits resources**: `~/.cargo/config.toml`; `~/.factory/sessions/` (read-only; fixtures are copies
redacted by `scripts/redact-fixture.sh` (emails, `/home/user` paths; originals stay outside the repo under
`~/.droid-observatory/originals/<slug>/` with SHA-256 recorded), committed only after `gitleaks detect --no-git`
is clean on the redacted files and they were read by a reviewer; owner decision 12); the owner's
Docker, Ollama and SurrealDB services; keychain values (read through `core::secrets` or
`security find-generic-password -s <service>` WITHOUT `-w`; never print, log, or copy them); the live Grafana
stack beyond the M5 export test; GitHub Issues (none are created: backlog is `BACKLOG.md` only).

**Outward writes allowed**: pushes of `mission/**`, `wt/**`, `demo/**` branches; M4 demo infrastructure via
`gh` (`demo/base`, label `demo:red`, ruleset `demo-gate`, PRs `demo/*` → `demo/base`); the final PR by the
orchestrator. Nothing else leaves the machine.

Workers: if your feature cannot be completed inside these boundaries, hand off with
`returnToOrchestrator: true` and say why. Never violate a boundary to finish.

## Mission Directives

**Tools**: `make check` is the only local gate (same as CI `mission-checks`). `cargo llvm-cov -p
observatory-core --fail-under-lines 80` from M0 (run alone). `agent-browser` 0.37.1 for the browser host on
3141. `gh` 2.102 (owner's auth) for GitHub reads and the demo pair. `sqlite3` for the store. `actionlint`,
`gitleaks`, `markdownlint-cli2`, `lychee` through the Makefile.

**Skills**: `core-worker`, `ui-worker`, `infra-worker`, `integration-worker` as assigned per feature; each
worker invokes its skill after `mission-worker-base`. Validators follow `library/user-testing.md`.

**Dependencies** (versions verified 2026-10-22, table in `architecture.md` §13): Rust 1.99.1; tauri 2.12.5,
tauri-cli 2.12.4, leptos 0.8.22 (csr), trunk 0.22.0, notify 8.2.0, serde 1.0.229, serde_json 1.0.154,
rusqlite 0.40.2 (bundled), tokio 1.54.1 (app/host only), keyring-core 1.0.1 + apple-native-keyring-store 1.0.2
(never `keyring` 4.x), opentelemetry* 0.33.1, tracing-opentelemetry 0.34.0, tracing 0.1.44,
tracing-subscriber 0.3.23, cargo-llvm-cov 0.9.1, cargo-machete 0.9.2, cargo-deny 0.20.2. Any other crate:
version verified on the day, `make deny` green, noted in the handoff.

**Owner decisions after the spec** (binding; full text in `planning-notes.md`):
1. Mapping version is selected from the Droid version in the fixture `.capture.json` header; usage, model,
   tags and child links come from the sibling `<id>.settings.json`.
2. Keyring variant B (above). 3. DMG only in CI. 4. Tauri window is a smoke check; the browser host is the
   primary interactive surface; the owner adds one unlocked-display screenshot per integration.
5. Concurrency limits (below). 6. GitHub token is a read-only fine-grained PAT: read checks through Actions
   runs and commit statuses, never the check-runs API. 7. M4 exit: Merge button visible when policy allows;
   the app surfaces the 403 cleanly; the owner merges; the badge updates from the poll.
8. At a usage throttle or a milestone cap the run pauses, usage so far is written to `reports/usage/`, the
   stall flag goes up and the owner is asked; no model/effort downgrade. 9. Backlog is `BACKLOG.md` only.
10. (2026-10-23, owner) INVARIANT: the models and efforts defined at mission approval never change for the
   lifetime of the mission. When a Factory usage limit is reached the mission STOPS. No worker,
   validator or orchestrator turn runs on a fallback/core model (e.g. `kimi-k3`); the overage preference is
   "stop", never "switch". Before any resume the owner restores the mission model settings
   (`model-settings.json`: workers `claude-sonnet-5-5`, validators `claude-opus-5-5`, both `high`) and the
   orchestrator verifies them; a worker that started on a wrong model is restarted from scratch, not
   resumed. Once correct, `model-settings.json` is protected with `chflags uchg` (done 2026-10-23 09:4x
   local; `ls -lO` shows `uchg`); a deliberate change is `chflags nouchg`, edit, `chflags uchg`, plus a
   decision file. Every such episode is recorded in the session log; the policy is decision file D-0NN (written at
   S integration) and a rule in `ai/RULES.md`. Episode 1: worker session `82a61cf6` for `m0-integrate-s`
   started on `kimi-k3` at 2026-10-23T06:40:42Z, ended with an error at 07:13:30Z, zero commits; the model
   of the resumed user-testing-validator-s session (`d0304e2e`, resumed 06:40Z) is not recorded.
11. (2026-10-23, owner) COMMUNICATION: think as much as you need, say little. To the human: one line of

# droid-observatory mission (mission id e194b9e3-6a67-42b9-bfc9-dd4e1ac23b0c).

# Concurrency rules (measured 2026-10-22, reports/readiness/2026-10-22-validation-readiness.md,

#   - `cargo llvm-cov` runs alone (1-min load 3.3 -> 14.6 on 10 cores during the scratch run);
#     it builds under $CARGO_TARGET_DIR/llvm-cov-target, so it does not wait on the build lock
#     and competes for CPU instead.

#     "Blocking waiting for file lock on build directory" is a wait, not a failure.
#   - Exactly one `trunk serve` owns port 3141. `cargo tauri dev` starts its own trunk on 3141

#   - Cold `trunk serve` 55.94 s, incremental 1.46-2.08 s, `cargo tauri dev` to running app 37.66 s.
#   - Validators run user tests only after builds finish.
#
# Ports: 3141 = UI dev server (one trunk at a time); 3142-3149 = scratch (a second trunk, a
# test HTTP server, etc.). Off-limits: 5000, 7000, 8000, 11434, 18444-18451 and anything already

# Machine: 10 cores, 64 GB RAM, baseline 1-min load 3-10 (readiness run: `load averages: 3,05 6,26 9,34`).

  COVERAGE_MIN: "80"
  # Shared build directory; comes from the login shell environment (not ~/.cargo/config.toml).
  # Listed here so a runner that scrubs the environment reproduces the same lock behaviour.
  CARGO_TARGET_DIR: /home/user/.cargo/shared_rust_target

  OBSERVATORY_LOG: info

    # Stop trunk-ui first: exactly one trunk may own 3141. The trunk this service starts also serves
    # agent-browser validators on 3141.
    start: cd /home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/observatory-wt/current && make app-dev > /tmp/observatory-tauri.log 2>&1
    # Killing cargo-tauri alone orphans `trunk serve` and the app binary (both reparent to PID 1 and

    # The debug binary is $CARGO_TARGET_DIR/debug/observatory-app (package name, not productName).
    stop: >-

      sleep 1;
      lsof -ti :3141 | xargs kill 2>/dev/null;

    # cargo colours the log (`\e[1m\e[92m     Running\e[0m`), so strip ANSI codes before grep (user-testing-validator-s).
    healthcheck: >-

    log: /tmp/observatory-tauri.log
    port: 3141
    depends_on: []

# Integration and boundaries

**What belongs here:** the worktree lifecycle, the integration procedure step by step, the shared files only
the integration feature writes, the reports and session-log entries produced at each boundary, how usage is
measured and priced, the budget caps and throttle behaviour, and what the human answers. Sources:
`planning-notes.md` "Execution model" and notes 8-9, `architecture.md` §16, `SPEC.md` §2, §9, §10,
`reports/README.md`, `ai/session/2026-10-22-session.md` entries 24-26, `config/prices/2026-10-22.toml`.

**What does not belong here:** CI job definitions and how to read runs (`github-and-ci.md`), test procedures
(`user-testing.md`).

## Paths and names

- Repository (mission branch `mission/observatory-v1`): `/home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/droid-observatory`
- Worktrees: `/home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/observatory-wt/<m>` on branch `wt/<m>`, `<m>` in
  `s, m0, m1, m2, m3, m4, m5`.
- Stable symlink used by `services.yaml`: `/home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/observatory-wt/current`.
- Workers and validators of `<m>` edit only inside `wt/<m>`. Two worktrees never edit the same file (rule 13).

## Worktree lifecycle (commands)

Create the worktree for milestone `<m>` (orchestrator at mission start for S; the integration feature for
every later milestone):

```sh
REPO=/home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/droid-observatory
WT_ROOT=/home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/observatory-wt
mkdir -p "$WT_ROOT"
git -C "$REPO" worktree add "$WT_ROOT/<m>" -b "wt/<m>" mission/observatory-v1
ln -sfn "$WT_ROOT/<m>" "$WT_ROOT/current"
git -C "$WT_ROOT/<m>" branch --show-current        # wt/<m>
sh /home/user/.factory/missions/e194b9e3-6a67-42b9-bfc9-dd4e1ac23b0c/init.sh   # verifies hooks, branch, symlink
```

Workers commit on `wt/<m>` and push it (`git -C "$WT_ROOT/<m>" push -u origin "wt/<m>"`); `mission-branch.yml`
does not run on `wt/**`, so `make check` in the worktree is the worker's gate. Remove the worktree only after
integration (its branch stays as history):

```sh
git -C "$REPO" worktree remove "$WT_ROOT/<prev>"
git -C "$REPO" worktree prune
```

## Integration procedure (integration feature, first feature of each milestone after S)

Skill `integration-worker`; runs on the mission branch in the repository checkout, never in a worktree.

1. Preconditions: the previous milestone's validators passed with zero blocking findings; `make check` is
   green in `wt/<prev>`; `wt/<prev>` is pushed.
2. Merge, no fast-forward:

   ```sh
   cd /home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/droid-observatory
   git status --short            # clean, on mission/observatory-v1
   git merge --no-ff wt/<prev> -m "Integrate <prev>: <one line of what landed>"
   ```

   A conflict means rule 13 was violated: resolve it in a new commit on the mission branch and record it in
   the boundary report (`docs/runbooks/stalled-mission.md`, `integration.conflict`).
3. `make check` on the mission branch (exit 0 required). From M0 also `cargo llvm-cov -p observatory-core --fail-under-lines 80`, alone.
4. Decision files due at this boundary (`docs/decisions/D-NNN-slug.md` with `**Date:**`, `**Status:**`,
   context, decision, alternatives, consequences), then `make decisions-index`. Due at S integration:
   session schema and mapping input (fixture header carries `droid --version`; sidecar for usage and children),
   keyring variant B, backlog is `BACKLOG.md` only, coverage, machete, read-only token (Actions runs and
   commit statuses instead of Checks).
5. Shared files, written only here: `SPEC.md` §9 (one `F-NNN` row per owner feedback, with date, applies-to,
   status) and §10 (one row per integrated milestone: integrated date, what landed, tests green, usage spent,
   deviations, unknown events left), `SPEC.md` amended as-built where a note or decision changed it (rule 8),
   `README.md`, `BACKLOG.md` (new `B-NNN` rows with reason and earliest; settled rows marked done with the
   date, dropped rows struck through), `docs/decisions/README.md` (generated), `reports/usage/<m>.md`,
   `reports/readiness/<date>-<m>.json`, `reports/ci/<date>-<m>.md`, `reports/README.md` index lines.
6. Session log entry in `ai/session/<date>-session.md` (style below), and `build-log/<day>/*.jsonl` committed
   as they are.
7. Commit (subject at most 72 characters, co-author trailer), push `mission/observatory-v1`, wait for
   `mission-checks` green (`gh run watch`, then `gh run view <id> --json createdAt,updatedAt,conclusion` for
   the wall time); paste the run id and times into `reports/ci/<date>-<m>.md` (one more commit if the report
   is written after the run; the second push produces a second run, which is noted).
8. Record the owner's unlocked-display screenshot path in the boundary report (the owner takes it at this
   boundary, planning note 4).
9. Remove the old worktree, create `wt/<next>`, repoint `current` (commands above), run `init.sh`.
10. Return the boundary report to the orchestrator: what landed, tests green, `make check` and
    `mission-checks` results with ids, usage spent against the cap, deviations proposed with reason and cost,
    unknown events left, decisions written, open questions for the owner. The human answers only here or
    when the stall flag is up (rule 15).

Final M5 integration and the single PR `mission/observatory-v1` to `main` are the one feature of milestone
`final` (`integration-worker`, `final-integrate-m5-and-open-pr`): it also writes `reports/waste/m5.md` with
`observatory-cli metrics` on the mission's own capture and verifies the Process section of the contract
(VAL-PROC-001..037). It opens the PR, waits for `gate`, confirms `mergeStateStatus CLEAN` and hands over; the
owner merges and the branch is deleted at the merge.

## Reports at each boundary (`reports/README.md` conventions)

Numbers pasted from the tools that produced them (rule 7); the README indexes each file with a one-line
description.

| File | Content |
|---|---|
| `reports/usage/<m>.md` | tokens per role and model (input, output, cache read, cache write, thinking), Factory credits when visible, cost at `config/prices/2026-10-22.toml`, waste by cause, wall time of the milestone, the cap and the remainder; source named (usage page or `.settings.json` fields) |
| `reports/readiness/<date>-<m>.json` | Agent Readiness report re-run at integration (`/readiness-report`, B-015); existing: `2026-10-22-baseline.json` (Level 1, 5 of 65), `2026-10-22-scaffold.json` (Level 3, 31 of 65), `2026-10-22-actions.json` (36 of 66) |
| `reports/ci/<date>-<m>.md` | the `mission-branch` run on the integration push: run id and URL, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, wall time, per-job durations, warm or cold, against the 3-minute budget (SPEC §7, rule 11) |
| `reports/readiness/<date>-<label>.md` | prose findings (readiness-style) when a milestone produced measured facts worth keeping, e.g. attach latency or Leptos go/no-go evidence |

The owner's screenshot path for the milestone is referenced from `reports/usage/<m>.md` (or the boundary
report) with its byte size.

## Session log entry style (`ai/session/<date>-session.md`)

The file is excluded from markdownlint (`ignores: ai/session/**`) because it records text verbatim. Entries
24-26 set the pattern:

- Heading `## Entry N — <short title>` (em dash), numbered consecutively across the day.
- Bold lead-ins as paragraphs, in this order when they apply: `**Owner message (verbatim):**` or
  `**Owner answers (verbatim):**` as a bullet list quoting the owner word for word; `**Edits applied ...:**`
  listing each file and what changed in it; `**Shipping:**` (branch, target, who merges);
  `**Shipped:**` or `**Outcome:**` with bullets naming full commit SHAs and subjects, PR numbers with URLs,
  run ids with URLs and conclusions, pasted times (`wall time 9 min 19 s, pasted from gh run view`),
  per-job durations, `make check` exit code and what was skipped and why.
- Corrections to earlier entries are stated in the later entry ("Correction to entry 24: ..."), never edited
  in place.
- Owner decisions are listed with the artefact they produce ("decision file at S integration").
- Transcript pointers: the session ids of the workers involved
  (`Worker session 82ad1581-fe75-4436-ac9c-9bc1e20a789b (dependency readiness)`).
- The entry that introduces itself names its own commit ("Commit: the commit that introduces this entry").

## Usage measurement and pricing

Unit: USD-equivalent at `config/prices/2026-10-22.toml`, computed from token counts Factory reports for the
mission's sessions, pasted, never estimated (SPEC §2, rule 7). Factory Standard Credits (`factoryCredits`) are
recorded next to the cost when visible.

Sources, in order of preference:

1. The Factory usage page for the mission (paste the numbers and the page date).
2. The sidecars of the mission's sessions under
   `~/.factory/sessions/-home-user-code-EllyaOrg-projects-dalimaray-droid-observatory/<id>.settings.json`:
   `tokenUsage` (this session), `inclusiveTokenUsage` (session plus children),
   `childInclusiveTokenUsageBySessionId` (per child), each with `inputTokens, outputTokens, cacheReadTokens,
   cacheCreationTokens, thinkingTokens, factoryCredits`; `model` and `reasoningEffort` give the price row.
   Read them with `jq`, never copy the files. The milestone's sessions are the orchestrator session plus the
   children spawned during that milestone (`tags[name=subagent].metadata.callingSessionId`, `session_start`
   timestamps between the two integration commits).

Price table (per million tokens, USD, read from the vendor page on 2026-10-22, `verified = true`):

| Model | Role default | Input | Output | Cache read | Cache write |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `claude-fable-5.1` | orchestrator | 10.0 | 50.0 | 0.25 | 12.5 |
| `claude-opus-5-5` | validator | 4.0 | 20.0 | 0.20 | 5.0 |
| `claude-sonnet-5-5` | worker | 2.0 | 10.0 | 0.10 | 2.5 |
| `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` | (none) | 1.0 | 5.0 | 0.10 | 1.25 |

Cost per session = `inputTokens * input_per_m / 1e6 + outputTokens * output_per_m / 1e6 +
cacheReadTokens * cache_read_per_m / 1e6 + cacheCreationTokens * cache_write_per_m / 1e6`, by the session's
`model`. `thinkingTokens` are reported alongside; the table has no separate thinking price, so state how they
were treated (SPEC §5.6 metric definitions decide; until then list them unpriced). Sessions on a model absent
from the table (e.g. `gpt-6.1-sol`, seen in this directory) are listed with tokens and "no price row".

### Orchestrator cap (owner, 2026-10-23)

The orchestrator is capped per milestone at 20 % of that milestone's cap: M0 12, M1 30, M2 16, M3 12, M4 24,
M5 24 USD-eq (re-set at the M0 boundary together with the milestone caps). It is measured as the delta of the
orchestrator session's own `tokenUsage` (not `inclusiveTokenUsage`) from the baseline recorded in the previous
usage report; the baseline in `reports/usage/s.md` at the S integration is input 629 245, output 499 465,
cache read 32 674 587, cache write 3 520 336, priced 83.44 USD-eq mission-to-date. Each `reports/usage/<m>.md`
shows the delta, its price at the `claude-fable-5.1` row, the orchestrator cap for the milestone, and the new
absolute `tokenUsage` that becomes the next baseline.
## Budget caps (SPEC §2, owner planning numbers, re-capped at the M0 boundary)

| Milestone | Cap (USD-eq) | Reason for the size |
|---|---|---|
| S walking skeleton | 40 | thin slice, few files, mostly scaffolding and one fixture |
| M0 capture and mapping | 60 | mapper plus golden tests; the capture already exists |
| M1 board, replay, attach | 150 | largest UI milestone and the Leptos go/no-go; rework budget inside |
| M2 host | 80 | RPC adapter plus launch screen |
| M3 intervention | 60 | lane-7 semantics over M2 controls |
| M4 branch, gate, fix loop | 120 | two adapters, the demo branch pair, a live PR loop |
| M5 time, waste, cost | 120 | the metric engine and its oracle test; export; charts |
| Total | 630 | hard stop; the final PR and fixes come out of the unspent remainder |

Orchestrator share per milestone: 20 % of the cap (M0 12, M1 30, M2 16, M3 12, M4 24, M5 24 USD-eq), measured
as described under "Orchestrator cap" above; re-set at the M0 boundary with the milestone caps.

M0 re-cap step: at the M0 boundary the orchestrator proposes re-caps for M1-M5 from the measured S and M0
usage (`reports/usage/s.md`, `reports/usage/m0.md`); the owner accepts or changes them; the new table goes to
`SPEC.md` §2 with an `F-NNN` row in §9. Until then the table above stands.

## Throttles and caps (planning note 8)

At a Factory usage throttle (5-hour, 7-day or monthly limit) or at a milestone cap: the run pauses at the
point reached, usage so far is written to `reports/usage/<m>.md` (marked partial), the stall flag goes up and
the owner is asked. Spending beyond a cap is a deviation (rule 9) and waits for approval. **No silent model or
reasoning-effort downgrade, ever**: any model or effort change is a decision file (rule 19). Workers that hit
a throttle mid-feature leave the worktree in a committed state (red test committed, work-in-progress described
in the handoff) and report; nothing is amended or stashed.

## What the human answers at each boundary (SPEC §2, planning notes)

| Boundary | Question |
|---|---|
| S to M0 | decision files reviewed (session schema, keyring B, backlog, coverage, machete, read-only token); SPEC amended as-built. Answered 2026-10-23: communication rule, PII rule for fixtures, orchestrator cap, D-011 confirmed with addenda, hook `script` field, `reviewed_by` stays `factory-droid[bot]`, rule 14 wording (see "Pending integration edits") |
| M0 to M1 | re-caps for M1-M5 from measured S and M0 usage; "defined, not observed" kinds accepted; exact `Task` fields for roles and ids frozen |
| M1 go/no-go | board renders the M0 capture with at most 3 rework sessions after the first scrutiny pass and a clean `trunk build` from a clean checkout; else the Tauri + TypeScript (Svelte) fallback from M2 by decision file |
| M2 to M3 | JSON-RPC method names recorded in the M2 decision file (informational) |
| M3 to M4 | write-capable token for the Merge button, or keep the read-only PAT with the clean 403 and the owner merges; who creates the `demo-gate` ruleset |
| M4 to M5 | `reports/reference/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-m0.csv` with the §9 columns (B-008); missing = stall flag |
| M5 and final PR | Grafana screenshot with only the allowed labels; the six "must prove" items of SPEC §1; merge of the single PR when `gate` is green |
| any time the stall flag is up | a cap or throttle reached, a proposed deviation with reason and cost, a keychain item or GitHub permission the mission cannot create, a red `gate` |

The human does not answer style, naming, crate choice within SPEC §4, test structure, feature splits or
anything already decided in `docs/decisions/`; those go to `BACKLOG.md` with a reason or into a decision file.

How the human is addressed (owner, 2026-10-23): one line of status per milestone event; a decision request in
three lines (what, options, the orchestrator's recommendation) when rule 15 requires one; nothing else. No
narration of reasoning, no restating the plan; explanations go to the session log and the mission files.
Workers and validators report to the orchestrator through their handoffs, never to the human.

Applied by the integration feature at the next integration pass on the mission branch (procedure step 4 and 5):

- `ai/RULES.md` rule 21 and `docs/decisions/D-019-*.md`: the communication rule (one line of status per

- `ai/RULES.md` rule 14 wording: "everything else goes to `BACKLOG.md` with its reason".
- `make decisions-index` after the decision files; `SPEC.md` §9 rows for the owner decisions.

Note: `ai/prd/review-2026-10-22.md` was restored by the owner's decision (`git checkout`); SPEC §1 keeps
listing it. No edit is needed for it.

# Factory PostToolUse hook: append one compact JSON line per tool call to build-log/
# (ai/RULES.md rule 17). Records what was called, never the tool response, so the
# log stays small and cannot leak tool output.
set -u
input=$(cat)

day=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%d)
dir="$root/build-log/$day"

# jq error cannot leave an empty file behind.
line=$(printf '%s' "$input" | jq -c --arg ts "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" '{
  ts: $ts,

**Date:** 2026-10-23

# Rules

The rules this project inherits, adapted for a build run as a Factory Mission (orchestrator, workers, validators) with the human as owner. Derived from the artstudio set (14-oct-2026); rules that only made sense for a hand-run team are struck, not deleted, so the decision is visible.

1. **Tests before code.** No production code without a failing test that asks for it. Workers write the test first and commit it red; validators check that the red run exists in the log. Tests are the contract between the spec and the build.
2. **A walking skeleton first.** The thinnest end-to-end slice (core crate, canonical event model, `observatory replay` over one captured session, an empty board that starts) is on the mission branch before any milestone deepens its area, so every integration is checked by real acceptance tests.
3. **Versions verified, latest stable.** Every crate, tool and image is pinned to a version checked against the official source on the day it is added; the spec's version table says when.
4. **No secrets, no magic values.** Credentials only from the OS keychain or the environment, never in the repo, the store or the logs; every number (poll interval, stall threshold, price) comes from configuration with a stated default and a reason in the spec.
5. **Everything from a clean clone.** `cargo test`, `cargo run -p observatory-cli -- replay <fixture>` and the app build work on a machine that has only the Rust toolchain and the Tauri prerequisites; the README's commands are the ones CI runs.
6. **CI is a gate, not infrastructure.** Light checks on the mission branch: `cargo fmt --check`, `clippy -D warnings`, `cargo test`, the replay fixtures, `cargo deny` (advisories and licences), gitleaks. The full attested run on the one pull request into `main`: everything above plus Semgrep (SAST), Trivy filesystem scan on `Cargo.lock`, Checkov on the workflows themselves, an SBOM (`syft` or `cargo-sbom`), the Tauri bundle built on macOS, build provenance with `actions/attest-build-provenance`, cosign-signed artifacts, with the Trivy results and the SBOM attached to the release. It never deploys.
7. **Counts come off the tool.** Test counts, timings, token usage and scan results are pasted from the run that produced them, never estimated.
8. **The spec is as-built.** When the code and the spec disagree at the end of a milestone, the spec is updated in the same integration, with the reason in `docs/decisions/`.
20. **Models are invariant for the life of a mission.** The models and reasoning efforts defined when the mission is approved never change until it ends. When a usage limit (5-hour, 7-day, monthly) is reached the mission stops and waits for the human; it never continues on a fallback or core model, and the overage preference is "stop", never "switch". Before a resume the human restores the mission's model settings and the orchestrator verifies them; a worker that started on another model is restarted from scratch, never resumed. Every such episode is written to the session log (D-018).

Struck from the artstudio set: *tester, coder and reviewer as separate agents per team* (the Mission's workers and validators take those roles; if the validators prove weaker, custom sub-droids bring the split back, as a decision); *the 90-minute box* (replaced by usage budgets per milestone).

\# Output styles

Control how Droid structures and writes responses in interactive CLI sessions.

Output styles add response-writing instructions to interactive Droid CLI sessions. Choose a
built-in style or create a Markdown file for a personal, project, or shared team style.

\## Choose an output style

1\. Start an interactive session with \`droid\`.
2\. Enter \`/settings\`.
3\. Select \*\*Output style\*\*.
4\. Choose a built-in or custom style.

Droid includes two built-in styles:

 Use Droid's standard response style.

 Return short, direct responses without unnecessary detail.


The picker shows where each custom style came from, such as a user, project, or plugin. Your
selection is saved as the \`outputStyle\` setting in \`~/.factory/settings.json\`.

\## Create a custom style

Create an \`output-styles\` directory at the scope where you want the style to be available:

\| Scope \| Location \|
\| :\-\-\-\- \| :\-\-\-\-\-\-\- \|
\| User \| \`~/.factory/output-styles/.md\` \|
\| Project \| \`/.factory/output-styles/.md\` \|
\| Folder \| \`//.factory/output-styles/.md\` \|
\| Plugin \| \`/output-styles/.md\` \|

Droid loads direct \`.md\` children of each \`output-styles\` directory. Nested files and other
file types are ignored.

Each file contains optional YAML frontmatter followed by the instructions Droid should apply:

\`\`\`markdown title="~/.factory/output-styles/review-notes.md"
\-\-\-
name: Review Notes
description: Put findings before the summary
\-\-\-

Start with actionable findings, ordered by severity.

Keep the summary to two sentences.
\`\`\`

\`name\` appears in the picker and defaults to the filename without \`.md\`. \`description\` appears
below the name in the picker. Keep the Markdown body focused on response presentation.
Repository instructions, tool permissions, and user requests still apply.

 Droid uses the style content available when a session sends its first request. Start a new
 session to use edits to that style. Selecting a different style takes effect on the next
 request.

\## Scope and precedence

Output styles apply only to interactive Droid CLI sessions. They do not change responses from
\`droid exec\`, Automations, Missions, subagents, the Factory App, or web sessions.

Droid combines styles from the active settings hierarchy and enabled plugins. Higher-priority
sources win when the same style is provided more than once. The built-in \`Default\` and
\`Concise\` styles are reserved and cannot be replaced.

When Droid asks you to trust a working folder, review its style files before accepting.
Project and folder styles, including styles from project-scoped plugins, remain unavailable
until the folder is trusted.

\## Troubleshooting

 Confirm the style is a direct \`.md\` child of \`output-styles/\` with a non-empty body. Run
 \`/diagnostics\` to see the source path and validation error, including when a style exceeds
 the size limit. Diagnostics do not include the style's instruction body.

 Confirm the style still exists, passes validation, comes from a trusted folder, and belongs
 to an enabled plugin. Droid keeps an unavailable selection but uses \*\*Default\*\* until the
 style becomes available again.

 Configure the saved output style and other Droid preferences.

 Package output styles with reusable Droid extensions.

 Review interactive commands and headless output formats.

 See how organization, folder, project, and user sources resolve.

**Status:** accepted (owner decision 2026-10-23 at the S to M0 boundary)

## Context

sent long status messages. The owner has to read them between milestones and asked for a fixed,
short format. Rule 15 already limits when the human is addressed; nothing limited how.

## Decision

Think as much as you need, say little. To the human: one line of status per milestone event, a
decision request in three lines (what, options, your recommendation) when rule 15 requires one,
and nothing else. No narration of reasoning, no restating the plan; explanations go to the
session log and the mission files. Workers and validators report to the orchestrator, not to the
human.

# D-021: The tool-call hook logs a `script` field

**Date:** 2026-10-23
**Status:** accepted (owner decision 2026-10-23 at the S to M0 boundary)

## Context

`.factory/hooks/log-tool-call.sh` (rule 17) records `command`, `file` and `summary` for each tool
call. A `Script` tool call carries its code in `tool_input.script`, which none of those fields
holds, so the log showed that a Script ran but not what it did. Scrutiny at S could not use the
build-log as red-test evidence for work done through Script calls.

## Decision

The hook adds `script`: the first 200 characters of `tool_input.script`, or `null` when the tool
input has no `script` (any other tool, or a string or array `tool_input`):

```jq
script: (.tool_input.script? // null | if . == null then null else .[0:200] end)
```

Checked on 2026-10-23: a Script payload with a 300-character script logs a `script` of length
200 (`jq -r '.script|length'` prints `200`); an `Execute` payload logs `"script":null`; a payload
whose `tool_input` is a string still writes a line with `"script":null`.

## Alternatives

Log the whole script (rejected: unbounded size, and scripts can embed secrets or file contents
that the log was designed to leave out); log a hash only (rejected: not readable as evidence);
leave it (rejected: Script calls stay invisible).

## Consequences

The build-log grows by at most 200 characters per Script call. The hook still never records the
tool response. Scripts longer than 200 characters are visible only as a prefix; the session
transcript holds the rest. The hook file change is allowed by this decision (the mission
otherwise keeps hooks unchanged).

Run 39924948471 on wt/m0 (24e3b10) was green but took 4m24s; the workflow_dispatch rerun 39925522835 on the same sha took 4m50s (rust job 4m34s: apt 2m34s, rust-cache restore 1m33s, clippy+test 10 s once cached; the first run's apt step took 58 s). The Linux `rust` job in mission-branch.yml does not build the Tauri shell and installs no apt packages. It runs `make fmt-check`; `cargo clippy --workspace --exclude observatory-app --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings -W clippy::cognitive_complexity`; `cargo clippy -p observatory-ui --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`; `cargo test -p observatory-core -p observatory-cli --all-features`; `make replay-fixtures`. The shell is covered by the macOS `bundle` job (`make app-build`, run through gate.yml on the PR to main) and locally by `make check`, which still lints and tests the whole workspace. mission-branch.yml also triggers on push to `wt/**`, so a worktree push runs the same checks. scripts/check-ci-jobs.sh pins all of this (`make check-workflows`).

The shell crate gets no clippy -D warnings on Linux and no unit tests in CI; a shell-only lint regression is caught by `make check` locally and by the bundle job compiling it on macOS, not by mission-checks.
